notes: Q3 FY2026 (reported after close 2026-07-29): Scores segment revenue +41% YoY ($459M, B2B +49% on higher mortgage origination score pricing) — still comfortably above the bear kill-switch floor (15% YoY) and the base range (25-35%), technically clearing the bull threshold (>40%) on this one KPI. But total revenue ($674.2M, +26% YoY) missed Street (~$679-692M) and FY26 guidance, while raised, came in ~0.9% below consensus. GAAP EPS $10.45 (+41% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS $12.18 (beat $11.97 est, +42% YoY) both strong. Stock initially popped ~+9% intraday then reversed hard, closing -16.5% the next session ($1,373.08 -> $1,139.54) — a continuation of the multiple-compression story, not an earnings-quality problem. Scores growth itself decelerated meaningfully quarter over quarter (60% in Q2 FY26 -> 41% in Q3 FY26), which is likely what the market is extrapolating forward despite still-strong absolute levels. Separately, the FHFA/VantageScore bi-merge requirement that the original thesis's SIGNALS block referenced as a near-term catalyst ('bi-score live') has NOT gone live — it was expected Q4 2025 and has been postponed indefinitely to align with the broader (still-limited, approved-lenders-only) VantageScore 4.0 GSE rollout. That is a modest net positive for the bear kill-switch (no forcing function yet), but it also means the bull kill-switch's second leg (multiple re-expansion above 40x) is nowhere close — FICO's own forward multiple compressed further, to roughly 27x (using guide EPS) from ~29x last quarter, moving AWAY from the bull re-rating trigger even as the Scores KPI itself touched bull territory. That divergence is itself the story: the market no longer rewards a strong Scores print with multiple relief while the pricing/regulatory overhang is unresolved.
